accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes gender discrimination?
o: Male dominance in family and society
Equal treatment of men and women in public employment
Unequal treatment by society of men and women
Biological differences between men and women
accepted.x: Gender discrimination means unequal treatment by society of men and women. Biological differences relate to sex, while male dominance describes patriarchy.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact definition from closely related gender concepts.
accepted.sec: Gender concepts → meaning

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sex refers primarily to biological characteristics.
2. Gender refers to socially constructed roles.
3. Gender and sex are identical concepts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Sex is biological, whereas gender consists of socially constructed roles. Therefore, statement 3 is incorrect.
accepted.tq: Split the options by identifying the statement that reverses a confusable pair.
accepted.sec: Gender concepts → meaning

accepted.s: Patriarchy is best understood as a system in which
o: men hold primary power and status in family and society
women hold primary power in family and society
descent is traced only through the female line
all family decisions are taken collectively
accepted.x: Patriarchy denotes male dominance and the primary holding of power and status by men in family and society.
accepted.tq: Match the sociological term with its precise meaning.
accepted.sec: Gender concepts → meaning

accepted.s: Which of the following is regarded as an exception to the general pattern of patriarchy mentioned in the context of family and society?
accepted.x: Matrilineal tribes are identified as an exception to the general pattern in which men hold primary power and status.
accepted.tq: Test the exception rather than the general rule.
accepted.sec: Gender concepts → meaning

accepted.s: The term ‘Missing women’ was coined by
accepted.x: Amartya Sen coined the term ‘missing women’ to refer to the consequences of discrimination against women, including intra-household discrimination.
accepted.tq: Use the person–concept association without confusing it with other gender scholars.
accepted.sec: Gender concepts → meaning

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Uma Chakravarti — A Field of One’s Own
Gail Omvedt — Seeing Like a Feminist
Bina Agarwal — Land rights and A Field of One’s Own
accepted.x: Bina Agarwal is associated with land rights and authored A Field of One’s Own. Seeing Like a Feminist is associated with Nivedita Menon, while ‘missing women’ was coined by Amartya Sen.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure author–work pair and eliminate swapped scholars.
accepted.sec: Gender concepts → meaning

accepted.s: Gender mainstreaming refers to
o: measuring only women’s participation in elections
restricting welfare policies to women alone
assessing the impact of every policy on women and men
replacing all gender-specific laws with personal laws
accepted.x: Gender mainstreaming builds a gender perspective into policy-making by assessing the impact of policies on women and men.
accepted.tq: Apply the concept to a policy-making situation rather than relying on a keyword.
accepted.sec: Gender concepts → meaning

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes gender mainstreaming from a gender audit?
o: Mainstreaming concerns only biological differences, whereas auditing concerns only employment.
Mainstreaming is limited to personal law, whereas auditing is limited to criminal law.
There is no conceptual distinction between the two.
Mainstreaming is a Beijing strategy, whereas a gender audit checks whether policies and budgets affect women and men equally.
accepted.x: Gender mainstreaming involves building a gender lens into every policy and was adopted as a Beijing strategy. A gender audit examines whether policies and budgets affect women and men equally.
accepted.tq: Compare two closely related concepts by their function and scope.
accepted.sec: Gender concepts → meaning

accepted.s: CEDAW was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly in
accepted.x: The UN General Assembly adopted CEDAW in 1979. India signed it in 1980 and ratified it in 1993.
accepted.tq: Separate the international adoption year from India’s signature and ratification years.
accepted.sec: International commitments - CEDAW, Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India and CEDAW:
1. India signed CEDAW in 1980.
2. India ratified CEDAW in 1993.
3. India adopted CEDAW only after the Beijing Conference of 1995.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: India signed CEDAW in 1980 and ratified it in 1993. Statement 3 is false because both events preceded the Beijing Conference of 1995.
accepted.tq: Use the chronological relationship among signature, ratification and conference dates.
accepted.sec: International commitments - CEDAW, Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action

accepted.s: India’s reservation under CEDAW relates to
o: Article 29(1) concerning arbitration or the International Court of Justice
accepted.x: India made a reservation regarding Article 29(1), which concerns arbitration or reference of disputes to the International Court of Justice.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the reservation article from the articles carrying declarations.
accepted.sec: International commitments - CEDAW, Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action

accepted.s: Which of the following Articles of CEDAW were the subject of India’s declarations mentioned in the international commitments?
accepted.x: India made declarations concerning Articles 5(a), 16(1) and 16(2). Article 29(1) was associated with a reservation.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between a declaration and a reservation by checking the exact article numbers.
accepted.sec: International commitments - CEDAW, Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action

accepted.s: The Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action was adopted at the
o: First World Conference on Women, Mexico City, 1975
accepted.x: The Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action emerged from the Fourth World Conference on Women held in 1995.
accepted.tq: Match the declaration with the correct conference and year.
accepted.sec: International commitments - CEDAW, Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action

accepted.s: How many critical areas of concern are identified in the Beijing Platform for Action?
accepted.x: The Beijing Platform for Action identifies 12 critical areas, including poverty, education, health, violence, economy, decision-making, media, environment and the girl child.
accepted.tq: Recall the precise number in a named international framework.
accepted.sec: International commitments - CEDAW, Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT identified as a critical area in the Beijing Platform for Action?
accepted.x: The Beijing Platform for Action covers areas such as violence, economy and decision-making. Expansion of nuclear weapons is not one of its 12 critical areas.
accepted.tq: Find the unrelated item among a list of recognised agenda areas.
accepted.sec: International commitments - CEDAW, Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action

accepted.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for special provisions for women and children?
accepted.x: Article 15(3) enables the State to make special provisions for women and children.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific sub-clause rather than the broader equality provision.
accepted.sec: Constitutional provisions for women → content

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 14 embodies equality.
2. Article 15(1) prohibits discrimination on the ground of sex.
3. Article 16(2) prohibits discrimination on the ground of sex in public employment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Articles 14, 15(1) and 16(2) respectively provide equality, prohibit sex discrimination and prohibit such discrimination in public employment.
accepted.tq: Combine related constitutional provisions while checking the scope of each Article.
accepted.sec: Constitutional provisions for women → content

accepted.s: Article 39(d) of the Constitution relates to
o: renunciation of practices derogatory to women’s dignity
accepted.x: Article 39(d) directs the State towards equal pay for equal work. Article 39(a) concerns an adequate means of livelihood.
accepted.tq: Distinguish neighbouring Directive Principles by their exact wording.
accepted.sec: Constitutional provisions for women → content

accepted.s: Which constitutional provision directs the State to secure just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief?
accepted.x: Article 42 directs the State to make provisions for securing just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief.
accepted.tq: Match the constitutional Article with the specific welfare objective.
accepted.sec: Constitutional provisions for women → content

accepted.s: Renouncing practices derogatory to the dignity of women is a fundamental duty under
accepted.x: Article 51A(e) includes the duty to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.
accepted.tq: Separate a Fundamental Duty from Directive Principles and reservation provisions.
accepted.sec: Constitutional provisions for women → content

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 243D — reservation of seats and chairperson offices in Panchayats
Article 42 — reservation of seats in State Assemblies
accepted.x: Article 243D provides for at least one-third reservation of seats and chairperson offices in Panchayats. Article 243T relates to Municipalities.
accepted.tq: Use the local-body distinction between Panchayats and Municipalities.
accepted.sec: Constitutional provisions for women → content

accepted.s: Under the constitutional provisions described, Article 243T concerns reservation for women in
accepted.x: Article 243T provides for reservation in Municipalities, including at least one-third of seats and chairperson posts for women.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between Articles 243D and 243T by the institution concerned.
accepted.sec: Constitutional provisions for women → content

accepted.s: According to the stated implementation detail, the 33 per cent quota under the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam came into effect in the Jammu and Kashmir and Puducherry Assemblies on
accepted.x: The stated implementation date for the 33 per cent quota in the Jammu and Kashmir and Puducherry Assemblies is 17 April 2026.
accepted.tq: Separate the implementation date from dates belonging to personal-law and labour-law reforms.
accepted.sec: Constitutional provisions for women → content

accepted.s: The Hindu Succession Act, 1956 is associated with which of the following reforms?
o: Abolition of the female heir’s limited estate and equal inheritance for women
Mandatory registration of every inter-faith marriage under one uniform law
accepted.x: The Hindu Succession Act, 1956 gave women equal inheritance and abolished the female heir’s limited estate. Civil marriage irrespective of religion is associated with the Special Marriage Act.
accepted.tq: Distinguish personal-law reform from marriage and labour legislation.
accepted.sec: Personal law reforms - Hindu Succession (Amendment) 2005 and AP amendment, Special Marriage Act, Hindu Marriage Act

accepted.s: The principal effect of the Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005 was that daughters became
accepted.x: The 2005 amendment made daughters coparceners by birth and gave them rights equal to those of sons in coparcenary property.
accepted.tq: Test the operative legal change using the exact phrase ‘by birth’.
accepted.sec: Personal law reforms - Hindu Succession (Amendment) 2005 and AP amendment, Special Marriage Act, Hindu Marriage Act

accepted.s: Which State had already made unmarried daughters coparceners through its amendment before the national Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005?
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh made unmarried daughters coparceners through an earlier amendment. The Andhra Pradesh Assembly passed the relevant Act on 24 September 1985 under NTR.
accepted.tq: Identify the State-level precursor to the later central reform.
accepted.sec: Personal law reforms - Hindu Succession (Amendment) 2005 and AP amendment, Special Marriage Act, Hindu Marriage Act

accepted.s: The Andhra Pradesh Assembly passed its Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act on
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh Assembly passed its Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act on 24 September 1985 under NTR.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the date of passage from the later year of the national amendment.
accepted.sec: Personal law reforms - Hindu Succession (Amendment) 2005 and AP amendment, Special Marriage Act, Hindu Marriage Act

accepted.s: The Hindu Succession Act does not apply to
o: all persons belonging to Scheduled Castes
all women belonging to Scheduled Tribes notified under the Act’s exclusion
accepted.x: Section 2(2) excludes notified Scheduled Tribes from the application of the Hindu Succession Act. The Supreme Court held that this exclusion cannot be extended to tribals merely on the basis of their religion.
accepted.tq: Test the statutory exception and avoid replacing Scheduled Tribes with Scheduled Castes.
accepted.sec: Personal law reforms - Hindu Succession (Amendment) 2005 and AP amendment, Special Marriage Act, Hindu Marriage Act

accepted.s: In Vineeta Sharma v. Rakesh Sharma (2020), the daughter’s coparcenary right was held to exist
o: whether or not the father was alive on 9 September 2005
only if the father was alive on 9 September 2005
only if the daughter was married after 2005
accepted.x: Vineeta Sharma held that the daughter’s coparcenary right is by birth and does not depend on whether the father was alive on 9 September 2005.
accepted.tq: Reject the tempting but incorrect condition concerning the father’s survival on the cut-off date.
accepted.sec: Personal law reforms - Hindu Succession (Amendment) 2005 and AP amendment, Special Marriage Act, Hindu Marriage Act

accepted.s: The Supreme Court upheld the exclusion of Scheduled Tribes from the Hindu Succession Act on
accepted.x: The stated date of the Supreme Court decision upholding the exclusion of Scheduled Tribes is 8 October 2025.
accepted.tq: Match the judicial development with its precise date rather than the amendment date.
accepted.sec: Personal law reforms - Hindu Succession (Amendment) 2005 and AP amendment, Special Marriage Act, Hindu Marriage Act

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Special Marriage Act, 1954 — civil marriage irrespective of religion
Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 — equal pay for equal work
Hindu Succession Act, 1956 — regulation of night shifts
Equal Remuneration Act, 1976 — grounds of divorce under Hindu law
accepted.x: The Special Marriage Act, 1954 provides a civil marriage framework irrespective of religion. The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 deals with monogamy and grounds of divorce.
accepted.tq: Match each law with its subject and reject cross-subject substitutions.
accepted.sec: Personal law reforms - Hindu Succession (Amendment) 2005 and AP amendment, Special Marriage Act, Hindu Marriage Act

accepted.s: The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 is primarily associated with
accepted.x: The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 provides for monogamy and specifies grounds of divorce under Hindu personal law.
accepted.tq: Identify the subject matter of the personal law statute without confusing it with succession law.
accepted.sec: Personal law reforms - Hindu Succession (Amendment) 2005 and AP amendment, Special Marriage Act, Hindu Marriage Act

accepted.s: The Equal Remuneration Act, 1976 was enacted to provide for
o: equal pay for equal work and absence of sex bias in recruitment and promotion
accepted.x: The Equal Remuneration Act, 1976 addressed equal pay for equal work and prohibited gender bias in recruitment and promotion.
accepted.tq: Separate the employment-equality statute from maternity and marriage laws.
accepted.sec: Equal pay and work rights - Equal Remuneration Act 1976, Code on Wages, night shifts

accepted.s: The Equal Remuneration Act, 1976 was subsumed into the
accepted.x: The Equal Remuneration Act, 1976 was subsumed into the Code on Wages, 2019, along with specified wage-related enactments.
accepted.tq: Match the earlier statute with the labour code that absorbed it.
accepted.sec: Equal pay and work rights - Equal Remuneration Act 1976, Code on Wages, night shifts

accepted.s: Which of the following enactments was NOT absorbed into the Code on Wages, 2019?
accepted.x: The Code on Wages, 2019 absorbed the Equal Remuneration Act, Minimum Wages Act, Payment of Wages Act and Payment of Bonus Act. The Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017 was not among these four enactments.
accepted.tq: Find the statute outside the specific group of laws subsumed by the Code.
accepted.sec: Equal pay and work rights - Equal Remuneration Act 1976, Code on Wages, night shifts

accepted.s: The Code on Wages, 2019 prohibits wage discrimination on the ground of gender, including discrimination against
accepted.x: The Code on Wages prohibits gender-based wage discrimination and includes transgender persons within its protection. It also provides for a statutory floor wage.
accepted.tq: Apply the scope of an anti-discrimination provision to the protected category specified.
accepted.sec: Equal pay and work rights - Equal Remuneration Act 1976, Code on Wages, night shifts

accepted.s: The Code on Wages, 2019 also provides for a
o: reservation of one-third seats in Municipalities
accepted.x: Apart from prohibiting gender discrimination in wages and recruitment, the Code on Wages provides for a statutory floor wage.
accepted.tq: Test an additional feature of the statute rather than its principal prohibition alone.
accepted.sec: Equal pay and work rights - Equal Remuneration Act 1976, Code on Wages, night shifts

accepted.s: Under the OSH Code, 2020, women may work before 6 a.m. or after 7 p.m. when
o: the work is performed only in government offices
the employer gives permission without any further condition
they consent and prescribed safety safeguards are provided
the worker has completed ten years of service
accepted.x: The OSH Code, 2020 permits women to work during these hours with their consent and subject to safety safeguards.
accepted.tq: Identify the conditional permission instead of treating it as an unrestricted power of the employer.
accepted.sec: Equal pay and work rights - Equal Remuneration Act 1976, Code on Wages, night shifts

accepted.s: The Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017 provides for paid maternity leave of
accepted.x: The Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017 provides 26 weeks of paid maternity leave. Contract and fellowship researchers may fall outside its coverage in the stated context.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact statutory duration and distinguish it from other leave periods.
accepted.sec: Equal pay and work rights - Equal Remuneration Act 1976, Code on Wages, night shifts

accepted.s: Which category is specifically noted as often falling outside the coverage of the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017?
o: All women working in municipal bodies
accepted.x: Contract and fellowship researchers are noted as categories that often fall outside the coverage of the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017.
accepted.tq: Test the coverage limitation rather than only the duration of leave.
accepted.sec: Equal pay and work rights - Equal Remuneration Act 1976, Code on Wages, night shifts

accepted.s: All four Labour Codes came into force on
accepted.x: All four Labour Codes came into force on 21 November 2025. The Code on Wages (Central) Rules were notified later, on 8 May 2026.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the commencement date of the Codes from the later notification of rules.
accepted.sec: Equal pay and work rights - Equal Remuneration Act 1976, Code on Wages, night shifts

accepted.s: The Code on Wages (Central) Rules were notified on
accepted.x: The Code on Wages (Central) Rules were notified on 8 May 2026, after the Labour Codes came into force on 21 November 2025.
accepted.tq: Separate the date of rules notification from the date on which the Labour Codes came into force.
accepted.sec: Equal pay and work rights - Equal Remuneration Act 1976, Code on Wages, night shifts
